newsitem.title: GERMANY: German states report moderate November inflation.
newsitem.headline: German states report moderate November inflation.

text.p: The four German states that make up preliminary west German consumer price data reported moderate increases in inflation during November.

Each of the states on Monday and Friday said that consumer prices either fell during November or were unchanged from October. Three of the four states also reported year-on-year tame inflation growth of 1.3 percent.
The Federal Statistics Office is likely to report preliminary west German consumer prices later on Monday or on Tuesday.
Analysts believe the four state reports mean the preliminary west German inflation could show a 1.4 percent yearly increase, down from last month's 1.5 percent pace.
The state of North Rhine-Westphalia reported the largest increase in yearly consumer prices -- a 1.5 percent increase. Prices on a month-on-month basis fell 0.1 percent.
Bavaria and Baden-Wuerttemberg both reported month-on-month inflation declined 0.1 percent, but climbed 1.3 percent on a yearly basis.
The state of Hesse, which has the smallest weighting in the west German provisional report, said consumer prices were unchanged month-on-month and up 1.3 percent year-on-year.

Although the figures were slightly lower than expected, they had little impact on inflation-sensitive bond markets. The DTB December Bund future contract was down 11 basis points at 101.03 in afternoon trade.
